transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-13
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Anya (CSM); Eleanor, Rafael, Priya, Tom (Oxford Thermal)

Summary: quick renewal check-in to confirm uplift sizing for H2, discuss adding EU region and a staggered burst plan, and align on contract amendment timeline. Customer asked about private VPC/on-prem path and SOC2 audit artifacts. SE to run short regen bench with their prompt set.

Topics: capacity sizing, dedicated vs hosted fallback, geo-provisioning (EU), SLA implications, security docs/SOC2/KMS, pricing amendment timeline, benchmark cadence.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, we're at 52 minutes on the cal, uh quick intros — I'm Maya, AE — Liam is our systems engineer.
[00:12] Eleanor: thanks, Maya. Quick status — we hit about a 20% qtr increase in traffic, and the team wants to bring forward the Dedicated pool add for EU.
[00:22] Rafael: yeah, and the main ask is lower p95 latency in EU, we see tails on inference right now when seq > 1024, and we'd like to discuss burst capacity for marketing pushes.
[00:35] Liam: okay, so two threads — region add (EU) + burst/overcommit strategy. we did some estimations from your last usage dump — if we target p95 220ms for shorter seqs and 450ms for long seqs, you're looking at X reserved units, plus a 20% burst buffer; we can sketch dedicated nodes in eu-west and a fallback routing policy to our hosted tier if capacity is exhausted.
[00:57] Tom: sorry to interrupt — when you say "fallback", what's the expected user impact? will requests be slower or get retried?
[01:05] Liam: both, so default is graceful fallback: route to a slightly cheaper model variant or to hosted which has higher latency but keeps success rates high. retries are configurable, and we have KV cache warmers to reduce cold-starts, though note the "K V cash" — sometimes the prefix cache gets evicted if burst pattern is huge.
[01:25] Eleanor: that's okay as long as SLA degrades gracefully. procurement will want commitments in the contract about the failover behavior.
[01:33] Priya: on contract — we need a 12-month extension with a phased uplift: +30% reserved now, +another 20% in Q4. pricing needs to be locked for at least 9 months. can you support that?
[01:44] Maya: yes we can. We'll propose a staged commitment — initial top-up for H2, then commit window for Q4. I'll send a new pricing sheet and SOW. We'll also include a clause for geo-activation dates and a runbook for failovers.
[01:58] Rafael: one more question — data residency and encryption. We need to ensure EU data stays in EU region, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. Is that available in the Dedicated flow?
[02:10] Liam: yes, Dedicated supports customer KMS and VPC peering. For Private/on-prem, we have a package but that is a longer lead-time. For EU residency, we can pin model endpoints to eu-west and configure egress restrictions — but we'll need an on-boarding ticket to set up the VPC and KMS roles.
[02:29] Tom: and the SOC2 artifacts — our compliance team asked for a copy of your SOC2 Type 2 and system diagrams.
[02:36] Anya: we can share the SOC2 report and an ops diagram. I'll drop the security pack in the same Drive folder as the proposal.
[02:44] Priya: perfect. Also curious about billing granularity — can we get token-level breakdown by route? we want to tie marketing bursts to a different cost center.
[02:54] Maya: yes, Console supports route-level cost breakdowns and tagging. We can export per-route usage and set quotas. We'll include a sample export in the proposal.
[03:06] Eleanor: good. on the performance note, our devs want to run a regen workload with our prompt set so we can see variance. how soon can you run that?
[03:13] Liam: we can kick off a 48h regen test this week if you share prompts and a small seed set. I'll instrument latency histograms and token-cost metrics and share the spreadsheet link.
[03:24] Rafael: do you have perf numbers for quantized variants? we might be okay with slightly lower quality if it halves cost.
[03:31] Liam: we do, we have q8 and int4 profiles, but quality trade-offs depend on your prompts. The Optimize recommendations can run a quick simulation on your traces to suggest quant and batching settings. we'll surface expected token reduction and delta in rouge/metrics.
[03:48] Priya: also, any competitors to be aware of? some of our execs asked about GoliathAI — they pitched a flat per-req price.
[03:55] Maya: yep we know them; main differences are our dedicated runtime optimizations and the observability console — you'll get per-token cost decomposition which helps with chargebacks. Also fallback and canary rollouts are built-in.
[04:09] Eleanor: timeline: we need EU live by 2026-07-15 for a product launch. is that realistic?
[04:16] Liam: it's tight but doable — provisioning dedicated nodes in EU and configuring VPC + KMS typically takes 4–6 weeks once we have SOW and purchase order. If we start onboarding early next week and you sign the amendment, July 15 is attainable; we'll need access for network peering and IAM roles earlier.
[04:35] Tom: what about DR / failover across regions? if EU goes down, do we route back to US?
[04:41] Liam: yes, smart routing can failover to another region (higher-latency). we can set an explicit fallback to US-hosted tier or a different geo, but you should understand cost and latency implications.
[04:52] Priya: procurement asks: can we get a committed burst pool option instead of paying on-demand? bursts in marketing are predictable — monthly.
[05:00] Maya: we can do a reserved burst tranche: commit to a monthly burst capacity at a discounted rate. We'll include that in the pricing.
[05:07] Rafael: any limits to model pinning? we want to pin a specific open model version for consistency across envs.
[05:13] Liam: you can pin model versions per route; rollouts are supported by canary / A-B policies. there's also an automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant if pinned model isn't available, but we document that in the rollout policy.
[05:30] Eleanor: ok let's recap next steps before we run out of time.
[05:33] Maya: recap: 1) I will send updated pricing and SOW (include staged commitment and reserved burst) — due 2026-05-18. 2) Liam will run 48h benchmark with Oxford prompts — results shared (due 2026-05-17). 3) Anya will upload SOC2 and ops diagram to Drive folder. 4) Priya to comment on SOW (due 2026-05-20). 5) Tom to send internal latency/cost targets doc (due 2026-05-15).
[05:55] Priya: agreed. any blockers on Redwood side?
[05:58] Maya: nothing major — need the PO/SOW sign-off to start dedicated provisioning. we'll also need the network CIDR ranges for peering.
[06:07] Rafael: we'll get that over.

Notes/Artifacts shared:
- pricing sheet (link: drive.google.com/example/pricing_oxford)
- draft SOW (link: drive.google.com/example/sow_oxford)
- security pack / SOC2 (to be uploaded by Anya)
- perf benchmark template (link: drive.google.com/example/bench_template)

End of transcript.

Meeting close: 15:52 UTC — thanks all, follow-ups in Drive and via email.
